name: Srinath Ramakkrushnan
profile: IIT Madras mechanical engineer who co-founded Zetwerk, an Indian contract-manufacturing platform, in 2018 with IIT classmates incl. CEO Amrit Acharya. As COO he leads strategy/execution and directly drives growth of Zetwerk's energy and capital-goods businesses across India, the U.S. and Europe.
interesting_fact: He personally runs Zetwerk's energy and capital-goods businesses across India, the U.S. and Europe - a direct fit for an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups he was a manager in ITC Limited's crop development and buying division, then co-founder/head of supply at OfBusiness (OFB Tech) and head of supply sales at BlackBuck (Zinka Logistics). Named to Fortune India 40 under 40 (2023) and ET 40 under 40 (2024).
notes: Some directories mislabel him as CEO; Amrit Acharya is CEO. Only a general company contact email is published (no dedicated press email found).

name: Anand Arvind
profile: Enterprise-software veteran who co-founded Zenoti (Seattle/Hyderabad cloud software for salons, spas and fitness businesses, founded 2010) with Sudheer and Dheeraj Koneru. As Chief Product Officer he leads Zenoti's technology and product vision; previously VP of Products at SumTotal Systems.
interesting_fact: At SumTotal Systems he led development of a learning platform used by over 20 million users.
deep_cut_fact: Earlier in his career at Microsoft he contributed to Windows System Restore. He holds degrees from BITS Pilani and Ohio State University and an MBA from the Indian School of Business.
notes: Low public profile; Sudheer Koneru (CEO) is the company's public face. Zenoti press page: https://www.zenoti.com/press (no press email found).

name: Bobby Clayson
current_role: Founder, Crofter Market (former co-founder/founding engineer, TaxBit)
profile: Utah entrepreneur and self-taught software engineer (V School coding bootcamp) who co-founded crypto tax/compliance software company TaxBit in 2018 with CPA Austin Woodward; TaxBit later pivoted to enterprise and government customers and passed a $1B valuation. He has since left TaxBit and founded Crofter Market, an online marketplace linking consumers with local regenerative farmers.
interesting_fact: Austin Woodward recruited him after hearing his talks on blockchain and smart contracts at a Utah cryptocurrency investment meetup.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he worked as a wildland firefighter and in sales; he was the eighth employee (a B2B sales rep) at Utah startup SpinGo, where watching engineers inspired him to learn to code.
notes: No longer at TaxBit; now runs Crofter Market (profiled on MountainWest Capital Network's Winners' Circle podcast, Feb 2026: https://www.mwcn.org/?p=15719). No published contact found; best route likely via Crofter Market.

name: Kamil Bajda-Pawlikowski
current_role: Co-founder, Starburst (formerly CTO); no longer on the executive team per Starburst's leadership page
profile: Polish-born database engineer and Yale computer-science researcher who co-founded Hadapt (first SQL-on-Hadoop company, acquired by Teradata in 2014), then was Chief Architect at Teradata's Center for Hadoop working on Presto, before co-founding Starburst (enterprise Trino/Presto data platform) as CTO. Starburst now lists him as co-founder; Martin Traverso is CTO.
interesting_fact: Hadapt, the company he co-founded and served as chief software architect, was the first SQL-on-Hadoop company and was acquired by Teradata in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: As a Yale CS grad student he co-authored the 2009 VLDB paper 'HadoopDB: An Architectural Hybrid of MapReduce and DBMS Technologies for Analytical Workloads' with Daniel Abadi and Avi Silberschatz - the research that became Hadapt.
notes: Current operating role unclear; Starburst leadership page (starburst.io/about/leadership) lists him only as 'Co-founder' under Founders. PR contact is Starburst's agency (AirCover PR).

name: Fayez Mohamood
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Bluecore (acquired by Insider One, announced May 13, 2026; post-deal role not confirmed)
profile: Georgia Tech-trained engineer who co-founded New York retail-marketing software company Bluecore (originally TriggerMail, founded 2013) with Mahmoud Arram and Max Bennett and led it as CEO to unicorn status, serving 400+ brands such as Sephora, J.Crew and Ralph Lauren. In May 2026 Insider One announced it was acquiring Bluecore.
interesting_fact: Bluecore was sold to agentic customer-engagement platform Insider One in May 2026; at the time Bluecore served 400+ US enterprise brands including ALO Yoga, Sephora, Bloomingdale's and The North Face.
deep_cut_fact: He met co-founder Mahmoud Arram in freshman calculus class; the founders spent about four years on several failed consumer products before Bluecore grew out of a technical insight from one of them, and he was in Arram's wedding, held the day after their first seed round closed.
notes: After the Insider One acquisition (May 2026), check whether he remains in an operating role. No published press email found; Bluecore press page: https://www.bluecore.com/press/.

name: Roberto Kutic
current_role: CEO, Festina.ai (AI venture studio); co-founder and co-owner of Infobip
profile: Croatian mechanical engineer (University of Zagreb) who co-founded Infobip with brother Silvio Kutic and Izabel Jelenic and served as COO, helping grow it from zero to $1B revenue in 14 years without outside capital; it became Croatia's first unicorn in 2020. He left Infobip in mid-2025 (remaining a co-owner) and launched Festina.ai, building domain-specific AI agents.
interesting_fact: Infobip reached $1B in revenue within 14 years without any outside investment before taking $200M from One Equity Partners in 2020, becoming Croatia's first unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career at Uljanik in Pula, one of Croatia's largest shipyards, after studying mechanical engineering and naval architecture at the University of Zagreb.
notes: Left Infobip COO role in June 2025; best route is via Festina.ai ('Contact us' on site) or his LinkedIn, where he announced the venture.

name: Ni Fei
current_role: Co-founder, Quicktron Robotics (Shanghai Quicktron Intelligent Technology); current title not verified
profile: Shanghai Jiao Tong University PhD in mechatronic engineering and port-automation engineer who co-founded warehouse-robotics company Quicktron (Shanghai, est. 2014) with CEO Yang Wei. Quicktron builds AMRs and intralogistics automation; investors include Cainiao, KION and Aramco's Prosperity7. Company registry data shows him as a ~10.35% shareholder.
interesting_fact: Quicktron's 2020 C+ round of over $100M was co-led by forklift/supply-chain group KION and Saudi Aramco's Prosperity7 Ventures; Cainiao (Alibaba's logistics arm) is also a major shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: Before Quicktron he was director of the R&D center at ZPMC (Shanghai Zhenhua Heavy Industries) electrical company, where he led development of China's first generation of automated rail-mounted gantry cranes and port AGVs.
notes: Very low public profile; Chinese name 倪菲. Bio sourced from 36Kr PitchHub company profile (third-party compiled). Alive status not independently confirmed; no indication otherwise.

name: Lu Ruize
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (since Nov 2024), YXT.com Group (Yunxuetang, Nasdaq: YXT) - per filings under the name Xiaoyan Lu
profile: Serial software entrepreneur from Suzhou (b. 1969) who founded corporate-learning SaaS company Yunxuetang (YXT.com) in 2011 after founding earlier software, education and internet-service firms. YXT listed on Nasdaq in 2024; the founder-chairman took over as CEO in Nov 2024 and the company is expanding internationally under the Radnova brand.
interesting_fact: Before Yunxuetang he worked as a manager at Suzhou Materials and Equipment Trading Group (1995-98), then founded two software companies in 1998; YXT later served clients such as Tongrentang, Haidilao, Didi, Luckin Coffee and NIO.
deep_cut_fact: He has said founding Yunxuetang was not about money - 'I see it as my life's work' - and Chinese media compare his path to Lei Jun's: trained in software, started in traditional software, and re-entered a new industry after 40. He was also a deputy to the 13th and 14th Suzhou People's Congress.
notes: Name mapping: Chinese media call the founder 卢睿泽 (Lu Ruize); SEC filings name the founder-chairman 'Xiaoyan Lu' (legal rep 卢小燕), and IR materials 'Peter Lu'. Very likely the same person but not explicitly confirmed by one source. IR contact is ICR (agency). Deputy-to-congress detail from TMTPost profile https://www.tmtpost.com/trendmakers/417097.

name: Romain Moulin
profile: French robotics engineer who co-founded Exotec (Croix/Lille, launched 2015) with longtime friend and GE colleague Renaud Heitz. Exotec's Skypod system uses climbing robots for warehouse automation; a $335M Series D led by Goldman Sachs in Jan 2022 valued it at $2B. Moulin remains CEO, leading global expansion and next-gen Skypod launches.
interesting_fact: Exotec's $335M Series D (Jan 2022, led by Goldman Sachs Asset Management with Bpifrance and 83North) at a $2B valuation made it France's first industrial unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a sales engineer at a small French automated-forklift company, rising to technical manager, then worked on advanced robotic imagers at GE Healthcare, where he says he 'really learned what it takes to build a hardware product.' He has known co-founder Renaud Heitz for 20+ years.
notes: PR agency email (Hopscotch, France) is from an April 2024 joint release and may be outdated; UK releases (2025) list agency Spreckley. Exotec press page: https://www.exotec.com/press/.

name: Ilana Harkavi
current_role: Original founder of Il Makiage (1972); no current role found
profile: New York-based makeup artist who founded the Il Makiage cosmetics brand in 1972; it was known mainly among professional makeup artists. The brand was later bought by siblings Oran Holtzman and Shiran Holtzman-Erel, who relaunched it in 2018 as a digital-first, AI-driven brand under parent ODDITY (Nasdaq IPO 2023). No evidence found that she holds equity or a role in today's ODDITY.
interesting_fact: The brand name is an intentionally simplified spelling of the French word 'maquillage' (makeup).
deep_cut_fact: Under her, Il Makiage was known in professional circles for innovations such as windowed eyeshadow packaging.
notes: Likely a list mis-attribution: the $1-2B valuation reflects the post-2018 Holtzman relaunch (ODDITY), not the original founder. Almost no public information on her; alive status unknown. Consider Oran Holtzman (ODDITY CEO) instead if the goal is the unicorn's founder.

name: Jenn Knight
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, AgentSync (per company/podcast materials; latest title not re-verified in 2026)
profile: Salesforce-ecosystem engineer who co-founded Denver-based insurtech AgentSync in 2018 with Niji Sabharwal after building back-office systems at LinkedIn, Dropbox and Stripe. AgentSync automates producer licensing and compliance for insurers; it bootstrapped before raising from Craft Ventures and others and reached a $1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: AgentSync bootstrapped to early product-market fit and only began pitching VCs in March 2020; investors initially said insurance's $1.3 trillion market was 'not cool enough.'
deep_cut_fact: Without a CS degree, she began her tech career as LinkedIn's first Salesforce engineer, building its Salesforce engineering and solutions-architecture team; at Dropbox she migrated the company's ERP before its IPO, and earlier did consulting at Bluewolf.
notes: Has done many podcasts (FNO InsureTech ep. 275, The SaaS Podcast #426) - receptive to podcast appearances. No dedicated press email published; company newsroom at agentsync.io/newsroom.

name: Wu Zhicai
current_role: Founder & CEO, ABclonal (Wuhan ABclonal Biotechnology / 爱博泰克); also listed as President of ABclonal Technology (Woburn, MA)
profile: Founder (吴知才, often 'Zack Wu') of ABclonal, a Wuhan-based life-science tools maker (antibodies, enzymes, NGS library kits) founded in 2011 with a US arm in Woburn, MA. The company raised RMB 1.2B in a Dec 2021 Series D co-led by Sequoia China, Luxin Venture Capital and CMB International, after a RMB 600M Series C in 2020.
interesting_fact: ABclonal set up a US subsidiary as early as 2013 and later built a US R&D center and national sales network; by 2020 overseas sales were about 40% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He and his co-founders started ABclonal in 2011 with just RMB 50,000 in start-up funds; within a year it was selected for Wuhan Optics Valley's 5th '3551 Talent Program', and within three years it had over RMB 100M in assets.
notes: Chinese name 吴知才 (not 武). English press releases quote 'Zack Wu, CEO'; BBB lists 'Zhicai Wu, President' for the Woburn entity - very likely the same person. The listed email is a general China marketing inbox.

name: Noam Solomon
profile: Israeli mathematician and computer scientist (two PhDs, MIT math postdoc) who co-founded Immunai in 2018 with MIT alum Luis Voloch. Immunai maps the human immune system with single-cell multi-omics and AI (its AMICA database) to improve drug development, raising a $215M Series B and signing deals with pharma partners such as AstraZeneca.
interesting_fact: He entered Tel Aviv University at 14 and had a CS bachelor's by 19, then earned two PhDs (computer science and mathematics) before coming to MIT as a postdoc in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: As a second-grader who disliked school, he'd visit his family doctor for notes - and she would give him a riddle each visit, which he spent hours or days cracking; he credits this with his comfort being 'outside my comfort zone.' He also told an investor 'No' when asked if he knew how to map the immune system - and still got the investment.
notes: Frames Immunai's mission around reversing 'Eroom's Law' (drug development costs doubling every ~9 years) - a good podcast hook. Writes op-eds (Calcalist/CTech).
